data.source_text_main_point: Police raids and voluntary closures across Europe are dismantling major BitTorrent and ed2k link sites, proving that hosting such sites is illegal and exposing operators to prosecution, despite their claims of legal loopholes.

actors.name: MPAA
variations: trade association representing the interests of major movie studios based in the United States

statements.key_statement: European police raids and voluntary closures dismantle major P2P link sites, proving hosting is illegal.
statements.long_statement: Across several European nations, law enforcement raids and voluntary shutdowns have recently forced major BitTorrent and ed2k link sites offline, effectively dismantling these platforms. This wave of action serves as practical proof that hosting such sites constitutes an illegal act, directly contradicting the operators' previous assertions that they could operate within legal loopholes by avoiding centralized storage of infringing files.

statements.key_statement: SuprNova.org voluntarily closed its BitTorrent links after arrests of other admins and legal warnings.
statements.long_statement: Following reports of arrests for administrators of other prominent peer-to-peer sites and receiving formal legal warnings, the operators of the Slovenian-based SuprNova.org decided to voluntarily shut down the section of their website hosting BitTorrent links. While the site's discussion forums and IRC network will remain accessible, the platform will no longer distribute links to copyrighted files, a decision made to avoid further legal consequences in the face of increasing enforcement pressure.

statements.key_statement: The decentralized eXeem project was developed to eliminate reliance on centralized link sites.
statements.long_statement: To avoid legal problems linked to centralized link sites, the decentralized BitTorrent project eXeem, created by the makers of SuprNova.org, entered beta in late 2004. This project sought to remove the requirement for outside torrent link sites and trackers. It let users publish and share new files directly on the network without using dedicated servers. This approach tried to fix the legal troubles that caused the shutdown of its parent organization's link site.

statements.key_statement: Police frequently close unproven P2P sites by seizing servers, exploiting the operators' inability to fight legal battles.
statements.long_statement: While the legal status of peer-to-peer link sites remains unproven and no such operator has successfully been sued by copyright owners, law enforcement agencies across multiple countries are frequently closing these sites upon receiving accusations of copyright violations. This enforcement strategy relies on the practical reality that seizing the physical servers of these sites effectively destroys them, as the operators are typically volunteers running non-profit services who lack the resources to engage in extended legal disputes.

statements.key_statement: In 2002, BitTorrent launched as a peer-to-peer application built for quick, distributed file sharing.
statements.long_statement: The BitTorrent system, developed by programmer Bram Cohen and introduced in 2002, functions as a peer-to-peer file distribution tool that allows users to swap file portions with one another rather than relying on a single centralised server, a design that supports the rapid distribution of new files to large numbers of users across Europe and globally.
